purpose: Plan a primary route and distinct alternatives between two user-selected routable points or roads under a temporary or saved disruption.

execution_tiers.name: Disclosed two-way connectivity proxy
required_data: two grounded endpoints in the same weakly connected component
execution_tiers.claim: Retrospective connectivity and least-impedance screening when From/To orientation alone prevents a directed route

execution_tiers.name: Historical least-impedance route
required_data: positive travel time or speed plus length

execution_tiers.name: Temporary or saved disruption alternatives
required_data: a confirmed closure, slowdown or travel-time increase
execution_tiers.claim: Blue unchanged baseline plus orange and yellow lowest-cost feasible recommendations

mathematical_formulation.primary_route: p*_s = arg min_p sum_{a in p} c_{a,s}
mathematical_formulation.alternative_enumeration: Enumerate loopless paths in nondecreasing impedance with Yen's algorithm
mathematical_formulation.difference_filter: because the user-fixed endpoint roads are shared by definition, retain p_k only if the Jaccard overlap of internal road sets is no greater than the confirmed threshold for every retained p_j
mathematical_formulation.disconnection: return no route rather than inventing a penalty

primary_sources.citation: Dijkstra (1959), A note on two problems in connexion with graphs
Yen (1971), Finding the K shortest loopless paths in a network

Hu and Chiu (2015), A Constrained Time-Dependent K Shortest Paths Algorithm Addressing Overlap and Travel Time Deviation. International Journal of Transportation Science and Technology, 4(4), 371-394.
Jenelius, Petersen and Mattsson (2006), Importance and exposure in road network vulnerability

known_limitations: This is retrospective analysis, not live navigation or an evacuation instruction.
Without a hazard-risk field, recommended means least uploaded impedance. It does not mean safest.
Without OD demand, one chosen corridor does not predict network-wide travel behaviour.
If strict From/To direction fails inside one connected component and no confirmed one-way semantics are available, the result is explicitly labelled as a two-way connectivity proxy.
Ordinary points are never randomly snapped to a road.
Inferred mapped roads can be straight topology connections rather than surveyed centrelines.
verification: each retained alternative satisfies the reported overlap rule
route totals equal returned segment totals
